A_policy_name: Loi n° 2009-24 du 8 juillet 2009 portant Code de l'Assainissement
D_policy_objective: Establishes a single, harmonised sanitation code governing liquid sanitation -- domestic, industrial, hospital and stormwater effluent, excreta and septage -- replacing the previously scattered treatment of the topic across the Codes of Water, Hygiene, Environment, Urban Planning and Construction (Exposé de motifs). Its core objective is public-health and environmental protection through sewer/network standards, mandatory municipal sanitation planning, and wastewater treatment/discharge/reuse rules. It is not a plastics policy, but Art. L29 explicitly and directly names plastics: it formally prohibits discharging 'les ordures ménagères, les déchets plastiques' (household refuse, plastic waste) -- along with hydrocarbons, radioactive substances, paint residues, used oils and other harmful matter -- into public sewer collectors, on the basis that such solid/plastic waste would damage pipework, endanger maintenance staff or disrupt treatment plants. Art. L46 separately prohibits dumping anything other than rainwater (which would include street litter and plastic debris) into stormwater drainage systems -- the principal pathway by which land-based plastic litter reaches rivers, the coast and the ocean. This is precisely the 'strong indirect plastics relevance, especially leakage prevention' identified in the task brief.
H_policy_type_justification: Full Act of Parliament: 'L'Assemblée nationale a adopté, en sa séance du mercredi 17 juin 2009 ; Le Sénat a adopté, en sa séance du lundi 29 juin 2009 ; Le Président de la République promulgue la loi dont la teneur suit.' Adopted by both chambers of the (then-bicameral) Senegalese legislature and promulgated by the President, then signed 'Fait à Dakar, le 8 juillet 2009' by President Abdoulaye Wade and PM Souleymane Ndéné Ndiaye -> legislation, not an executive/ministerial instrument.
J_policy_sectors_list: sanitation, urban planning & construction, local government/municipalities, water resources, environment, health, industry, agriculture, transport/roads
N_policy_budget_text: Art. L12: 'Les dépenses afférentes à l'élaboration des plans directeurs...sont à la charge desdites collectivités locales. L'Etat peut y contribuer notamment au moyen de son budget général ou de tout autre financement mis à sa disposition par des partenaires au développement.' Art. L73: 'Des taxes et redevances de rejet d'eau en milieu naturel sont perçues dans les conditions fixées par le Code de l'Environnement.' Coded 0.5 rather than 1 because the funding referenced is either a discretionary/non-ring-fenced general-budget contribution (Art. L12, 'peut') or an explicit cross-reference to the Code de l'Environnement's own (separately ring-fenced) pollution-tax/fund regime, already coded under Loi n° 2001-01/2023-15 elsewhere in this series, rather than a dedicated fund created by this Code itself.
R_instrument_description: Art. L29-L30: 'Il est formellement interdit de déverser dans les collecteurs publics d'eaux usées : ... les ordures ménagères, les déchets plastiques, les hydrocarbures, les substances radioactives, les résidus de peintures, les huiles usagées...' plus a long list of other harmful/incompatible substances (acids, cyanides, flammable materials, matter above 30°C or outside pH 5.5-8.5, animal waste, non-pretreated industrial effluent, etc.). Art. L30 clarifies the list 'n'est pas limitative' and can be extended by further texts.
U_instrument_implementation_text: Authority: 'Les agents assermentés du service de l'assainissement' are explicitly empowered (Art. L30) (+0.25). Enforcement: violations not otherwise specifically penalised fall under the general catch-all penal clause, Art. L105 ('Quiconque contrevient aux dispositions de la présente loi non assorties de peines correctionnelles...est passible des peines prévues aux articles 2 et 3 du Code des contraventions') (+0.25). Monitoring: 'Les agents assermentés...ont la possibilité d'effectuer chez tous les usagers, des prélèvements de contrôle afin de vérifier la nature des rejets envoyés dans les collecteurs publics' (Art. L30) (+0.25). Unconditional: the prohibition is stated in absolute terms ('Il est formellement interdit') with no exemption identified (+0.25).
W_comments: The single most directly plastics-relevant provision in this Code, satisfying Plastics Relevance Filter criterion (a) explicitly (not merely (b)/(c)) -- 'les déchets plastiques' is named alongside household refuse as a banned sewer input. This is precisely the provision the task brief highlighted.

L46: 'Les ouvrages du domaine public destinés à la collecte et à l'évacuation des eaux pluviales ne peuvent recevoir que des eaux d'origine pluviale...Les déversements, écoulements, dépôts, jets de substances autres que celles-ci y sont donc interdites; sauf autorisation du service chargé de l'assainissement.' D_policy_objective: Establishes a single, harmonised sanitation code governing liquid sanitation -- domestic, industrial, hospital and stormwater effluent, excreta and septage -- replacing the previously scattered treatment of the topic across the Codes of Water, Hygiene, Environment, Urban Planning and Construction (Exposé de motifs). Its core objective is public-health and environmental protection through sewer/network standards, mandatory municipal sanitation planning, and wastewater treatment/discharge/reuse rules. It is not a plastics policy, but Art. L29 explicitly and directly names plastics: it formally prohibits discharging 'les ordures ménagères, les déchets plastiques' (household refuse, plastic waste) -- along with hydrocarbons, radioactive substances, paint residues, used oils and other harmful matter -- into public sewer collectors, on the basis that such solid/plastic waste would damage pipework, endanger maintenance staff or disrupt treatment plants. Art. L46 separately prohibits dumping anything other than rainwater (which would include street litter and plastic debris) into stormwater drainage systems -- the principal pathway by which land-based plastic litter reaches rivers, the coast and the ocean. This is precisely the 'strong indirect plastics relevance, especially leakage prevention' identified in the task brief.
